notes: The reference game was unknown to me, and the author described it as a compact lane-defence field rather than an open world or free-for-all arena, which is Strategy's tower-defense case: waves walk fixed lanes toward something you defend while you place units beside them. Shape is lane-actor-track, worded here as the straight parallel garden rows waves advance along, and its P6 is a structural law - the route has to be continuous and unambiguous or the waves have nowhere to walk - so it is not overridable even though the field is small. Preset is Tower Defense with buildzone-grid as the plantable lawn tiles flanking each row, tracker-core as the base at the defended end, and spawner-npc as the wave mouth at the far edge; I dropped choke-bottleneck because a uniform lawn of equal rows has no pinch point. I decided the player walks the field rather than looking down on it as a board, so this is not a SET, and the grassy colourful cartoon styling is set dressing over one compact arena with every lane in view.
